messages.text: Why you don't direct update the links into "Try it: scroll the real pages" section ?
Leader, let's investigate this, do workaround more proper and find the longer-term fixes.

Found a likely cause; a tool fix is under way.
- Cause: our page server marks the changed countdown stylesheet as 'never changes, keep it for a year'. On a port that served an earlier version, Arc keeps the old copy, even after a reload. Fresh ports have no old copy, so they work. Best guess (not proven on your Arc), but the header is real: I checked it.
- Workaround now: use the 5422/5423 links in the PR text. The Try-it button moves to fresh, correct pages with the fix.
- Long-term fix (ts-i131, incident I-131): the server stops sending 'keep for a year' for any file that can change between builds, and pages that already went stale get cleared. It also checks whether any iPhone test loaded a stale file.
- Why the links weren't simply swapped: the Try-it section serves its pages through the console's own servers, which take no typed-in link. The fix makes those servers right instead.
What you need to do: nothing. I'll reply here when it's live.

Yes, it is fixed, and live since 11:12Z.

- Cause: our page server told the browser 'keep this file for a year'. On a reused port, Arc kept the old build's files.
- Fix (incident I-131, commit c7427cd0e9): the server now asks the browser to re-check every file, and a new port is used for each Try-it page.
- Also landed 11:1xZ+: Try-it pages are now served by one on-demand host (commit 51fb199f, from your T-106).
- Side effect: phone reload runs re-check about 51 files, so phone numbers from before and after do not compare.

What you need to do: if a Try-it page still looks old, tell me the page and I will check it.
